chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام looked at some people on the day of Fiṭr playing and laughing, so he said to his companions, turning toward them:

Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made the month of Ramaḍān a racetrack for His creation, in which they race through obedience to Him toward His good pleasure. So some people went ahead in it and won, while others fell behind and failed.

So how astonishing, utterly astonishing, is the one who laughs and plays on the day in which the doers of good are rewarded and the deficient ones fail. By Allah, if the covering were removed, a doer of good would be occupied by his good, and an evildoer by his evil.

key_terms.اَلْغِطَاءُ: the veil or covering over hidden realities
key_terms.اَلْمُحْسِنُونَ: those who do good and excel in righteous action
key_terms.اَلْمُقَصِّرُونَ: those who fall short and are negligent in their duties
key_terms.بِإِحْسَانِهِ: with his good conduct and righteous deeds
key_terms.رَمَضَانَ: the month of fasting presented here as the period of spiritual striving
key_terms.مِضْمَاراً: a racetrack or course of competition, meaning a field for striving in obedience

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Ḥasan عليه السلام say about laughing and playing on ʿEid al-Fiṭr?
ai.summary: This hadith portrays the month of Ramaḍān as a course of spiritual competition in obedience to Allah. On ʿEid al-Fiṭr, Imam al-Ḥasan عليه السلام reproaches heedlessness and amusement, reminding people that this is a day when the righteous are rewarded and the negligent suffer loss, and that true awareness of unseen realities would fully occupy each person with the consequences of his deeds.
